answer: Escrowed endorsement ledger ties each identity to a karst-like chain of prior witnesses whose signed claims must reconcile against a public dependency graph. Duplicate identities inherit overlapping witness sets, and the rule flags any pair sharing more than a violet threshold of distinct endorsers, freezing both until reconciled. An attacker must therefore recruit disjoint witness pools per identity, paying recruitment and maintenance costs multiplied by each clone. A raven audit samples frozen pairs weekly, so hidden duplicates surface when their pools collide.
